name: Vow
tagline: A programming language for LLM authors, with every contract proved by Z3
target: Coding agents writing software whose contracts, refinements and termination are machine-checked, and the people who review their work by reading contracts instead of bodies

log.summary: From spec to self-hosting in a day: a Rust bootstrap compiler (lexer, parser, type and effect checker, C code generation, Z3 verifier with refinements, contracts, invariants and counterexamples, verification cache), then a self-hosted compiler written in Vow that compiles itself to identical C. Guides for LLMs and humans, CI on macOS and Linux, quantified specs and termination measures, std/text.vow, benchmarks, reference counting with in-place updates, HashMap, generics with Result and try (and the Rust bootstrap frozen at the v0.3 language). vowsite, a verified static site generator, was built by OpenAI Codex from the docs alone and builds vow.kranzky.com. Released v0.1.0 to v0.3.0 with prebuilt binaries, install.sh and a Homebrew tap.

Specification language and tooling: structural ==, old(x), mutual and structural termination measures with a --totality report, recursive specification functions, field refinements assumed in goals, #line directives, Z3 pinned at 5.3.2, a verifier version enforced by SMT fingerprints, vowc fmt, vowc test, std/json.vow, vow-lsp (a language server whose hover shows what the verifier knows), Float, and more benchmarks. Released v0.4.0 to v0.8.0.

Modules (import as, selected imports, private declarations) and packages pinned to git commits (vow.pkg, vowc add, vowc fetch, a packages page on the site). Soundness work: a red-team pass with must-fail tests, --check-contracts (checked builds as the oracle), mutation fuzzing, cache and inout fixes, and docs/SOUNDNESS.md, a written soundness argument. Released v0.9.0 to v0.9.2.

Fixed six soundness bugs found by an independent review of the verifier against SOUNDNESS.md. Built tests/genfuzz.py, a random program generator whose surviving contracts are checked at runtime; it found and fixed one more bug. Runtime checks of recursive calls' measures, and SOUNDNESS.md extended to what the verifier relies on the type checker for. Released v0.9.3 to v0.9.5.

Refined type arguments (List<Nat>, Option<Nat>, Result<Nat, String>, Box<Nat>), checked wherever a value is stored and assumed wherever it is read, and refinements through generic functions (last(xs) on a List<Nat> is a Nat), validated by fuzzing with planted holes. Released v0.9.6. Closed the soundness follow-ups from the review: unambiguous field names in the SMT, measures may not call their own recursive group, structural measures in the cache key.

Added Vow to the Lean Machine portfolio as a labs project: project.json with history reconstructed from git, linked in via a symlink (project-026-vow -> ../vow). AI minutes are active time measured from the session transcript (gaps under five minutes); human minutes are estimated at about two per message.
